children: strong AI revenue growth is being accompanied by mounting margin and financing concerns as the cost of components and supply constraints weigh on the semiconductor company, according to Joe Albano of Tech Cache.

While Broadcom’s AI business continues to accelerate, Albano said the company is facing margin compression as higher DRAM, NAND and other component costs increase pressure across the AI infrastructure supply chain.

Albano said Broadcom’s outlook reflects strong demand for its custom AI accelerators, or XPUs, but cautioned that the broader financing structure behind the AI buildout warrants attention. With demand backing up in a supply-constrained environment, Broadcom’s guidance extending into fiscal 2028 is not necessarily surprising, he said.

However, the longer-term question is whether the companies funding AI infrastructure can continue supporting such high levels of spending if the anticipated returns from AI take longer to materialize.

A key concern for Albano is the increasingly interconnected financing model surrounding AI infrastructure. He pointed to the use of custom chips as collateral in some financing arrangements and questioned how fungible those assets would be if an AI customer were to run into financial difficulties.

Because custom XPUs are designed around specific customer workloads, their value could be less straightforward outside their original applications, potentially creating additional risks if funding conditions deteriorate.

The concerns come even as Broadcom benefits from the continued expansion of AI infrastructure spending. Albano's broader view is that investors need to look beyond headline revenue growth and consider whether the enormous capital being committed to AI can ultimately produce sustainable cash flows.

With major technology companies and AI labs committing increasingly large sums to infrastructure, the ability of the ecosystem to keep financing that spending could become a more important issue over the coming year.

For Broadcom, Albano remains cautious despite the strong underlying AI demand. He said the company could face a more difficult environment if the financing supporting AI infrastructure begins to weaken, particularly if expectations around the arrival of artificial general intelligence are pushed further out.
The result, in his view, is a stock where strong AI demand needs to be weighed against the sustainability of the spending and financing cycle supporting that demand.

title: Broadcom’s strong AI growth faces margin, financing risks
